jobs.title: Agile Program Manager
jobs.description: We're looking for an experienced Agile Program Manager to lead delivery across multiple cross-functional teams working toward a shared set of business outcomes. You'll sit at the intersection of strategy and execution: translating roadmap priorities into coordinated, predictable delivery, keeping dependencies visible, and making sure the right people are making the right decisions at the right time. This is a hands-on program role, not a status-reporting one. You'll own the cadence, the plan, and the risks across several Agile teams, and you'll be the person stakeholders trust to tell them where things really stand. What You'll Do Lead end-to-end delivery of a multi-team program, coordinating three or more Agile teams (Scrum, Kanban, or hybrid) toward shared quarterly objectives. Run program-level planning, including quarterly/PI planning, roadmap alignment, capacity planning, and release planning. Identify, map, and actively manage cross-team dependencies, risks, and blockers, escalating early and with clear options. Facilitate program ceremonies such as Scrum of Scrums, program syncs, system demos, and retrospectives, and make sure they produce decisions, not just updates. Partner with Product Owners and Product Managers to keep backlogs prioritized, refined, and aligned to business value. Build and maintain program-level reporting: delivery health, burn-up/velocity trends, OKR or objective progress, and RAID logs, tailored for both team-level and executive audiences. Drive continuous improvement in delivery practices, tooling, and team workflows, coaching teams and leaders on Agile principles where needed. Manage stakeholder communication across engineering, product, design, business, and leadership, keeping expectations aligned as scope and priorities shift. Track program budget, resourcing, and vendor or third-party deliverables where applicable. What You Bring 8+ years of experience in program or project management, with at least 5 years leading delivery in Agile environments. Proven track record managing multi-team programs (not just single-team Scrum) from planning through release. Deep, practical knowledge of Scrum and Kanban, plus experience with at least one scaling framework (SAFe, LeSS, Scrum@Scale, or similar). Strong command of Agile tooling such as Jira, Jira Align, Azure DevOps, Rally, or equivalent, including building dashboards and program-level reporting. Excellent facilitation skills: you can run a 50-person planning event as comfortably as a tense 1:1 escalation. Clear, concise written and verbal communication in English, with the ability to tailor the message for engineers and executives alike. Experience working with distributed or remote teams across time zones. Comfort operating with ambiguity: you can stand up structure where there is none and adapt it as the program evolves. Nice to Have Agile or program management certifications such as SAFe RTE, SAFe SPC, PMI-ACP, PgMP, PMP, CSM/CSP, or ICAgile. Experience with Agile transformations or introducing scaled frameworks into an organization. Background in software, SaaS, data, or digital product delivery. Familiarity with OKRs and value-stream or portfolio management. Experience in regulated industries (financial services, healthcare, insurance, public sector) where Agile delivery coexists with compliance requirements. Budget and vendor management experience on programs with multiple delivery partners. Our system identifies business opportunities through market signals, validates ideas with live ad tests, builds and launches software products, and brings in human experts wherever agents fall short. That loop already runs end to end: from idea to launched product to first revenue. Over the next 12 months, our focus is on reliability, throughput, and self-improvement, making every launch better than the last. About the role We're looking for a hands-on AI Engineer to take ownership of the architecture and development of our autonomous agent system. ð Build the data layer AI needs to do science

Application deadline: 16 Nov 2026 23:59 CET

About Claims

AI ate the Internet, but it can't digest science yet. A paper is thousands of words of prose written for humans, but an AI agent doing research needs to know what was claimed, what evidence supports it, and how far to trust it. Claims turns the scientific literature into exactly that: every claim, tied to its evidence, as structured data that models and agents can query.

We're a startup and run as Subnet 111 on Bittensor. Since our mainnet launch on 28 August 2026, an open competition of miners has processed more than 10,000 papers, and every record was checked by our validator before it entered the dataset. The competition keeps raising the bar: miners keep finding ways to beat our own reference pipeline, and every win becomes part of the standard the whole network is scored against.

The team

Claims was founded by two professors of economics and a senior engineer.

  • Philipp Koellinger, CEO, is a professor of economics and an experienced entrepreneur: founder of DeSci Labs and the DeSci Foundation, and co-builder of SciWeave with Ogban.
  • Christian Roessler, co-founder, is a professor of economics and game theorist. He designs the incentive mechanism that makes the miner competition work.
  • Ogban Ugot, engineering, is a senior backend and machine learning engineer. He built SciWeave, the Claims miner, validator and data pipeline, and you will work with him every day.

You would be the fourth person on the team and our second engineer.

Our culture

We are a fully remote team spread across Europe, Africa and the US West Coast. We have a flat hierarchy and move fast towards clearly defined goals. We think deep, don't shy away from difficult problems or conversations, and we ship relentlessly. The code you will write will run on a live network within your first weeks, and you own real things from day one. We are an AI-native company and expect you to be an AI-native Software Engineer we can trust.

About the role

Position: Software Engineer (Python, full-stack)
Location: Remote. You need to be able to join our team meetings in the afternoon, Central European Time.
Type: Full-time contractor. Start in December 2026 or January 2027.

We're looking for a Software Engineer to help maintain and build Claims and its supporting applications, services, and developer tools. Claims turns scientific research into structured claims and supporting evidence through document processing, AI pipelines, and automated evaluation.

This is a hands-on, backend-focused full-stack role. You'll work across Python services, web dashboards, data pipelines, integrations, and deployment tooling. Your work will combine delivering new features with debugging existing systems, improving reliability, and making the codebase easier to maintain.

You should be comfortable owning well-defined tasks from investigation through implementation, testing, and release, working with the team on larger design decisions and unfamiliar areas.

Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain Python backend services, APIs, command-line tools, and background processing workflows.
  • Develop and improve web dashboards and internal review tools using TypeScript, React, and modern web frameworks.
  • Maintain pipelines that ingest research papers, process documents, extract structured information, and evaluate results.
  • Integrate external APIs and AI model providers, handling validation, retries, timeouts, rate limits, and usage costs.
  • Work with relational databases and object storage, including schema changes, migrations, queries, and data integrity checks.
  • Investigate bugs and production issues across services, pipelines, and interfaces; address root causes and add useful regression coverage.
  • Help maintain deployment automation, continuous integration, logging, monitoring, and operational documentation.
  • Improve existing code through practical refactoring, dependency maintenance, automated tests, and code review.
  • Collaborate with engineering and research colleagues to turn requirements and experimental workflows into reliable software.

Required skills and experience

  • Typically 1â5 years of professional software engineering experience, or equivalent practical experience delivering and maintaining production software.
  • Strong Python skills, including building maintainable services or data processing applications, managing dependencies, and writing automated tests.
  • Experience designing, consuming, and troubleshooting HTTP APIs, with a sound understanding of JSON, validation, authentication, and error handling.
  • Working knowledge of TypeScript or JavaScript and experience contributing to React applications or a comparable modern frontend framework.
  • Practical SQL and relational database experience, including data modelling, migrations, and debugging queries.
  • Confidence working in Linux environments and using the command line to investigate logs, configuration, processes, and service failures.
  • Experience with Git, pull requests, code review, automated testing, and continuous integration.
  • An understanding of secure engineering practices, including access controls, secrets management, and careful handling of private data.
  • The ability to navigate an existing codebase, trace issues across components, and make focused, well-tested changes.
  • Clear communication, practical problem-solving, and the judgment to work independently while asking for input when requirements or risks are unclear.

Nice to have

  • Experience with FastAPI, Pydantic, PostgreSQL, Supabase, Next.js, or similar tools.
  • Experience integrating LLM APIs, building AI-assisted workflows, or evaluating model outputs for accuracy, reliability, latency, and cost.
  • Familiarity with PDF parsing, OCR, document extraction, scientific datasets, or evidence provenance.
  • Experience with distributed jobs, asynchronous processing, reproducible pipelines, or automated benchmarking.
  • Familiarity with Docker, Ansible, systemd, GitHub Actions, cloud hosting, or infrastructure automation.
  • Experience with Bittensor, decentralized compute networks, or systems for evaluating independently submitted code.
  • Exposure to Rust, native Python extensions, or WebAssembly.
  • An interest in scientific research, open-source software, and tools that make research easier to inspect and reuse.

You don't need experience with every technology listed. Strong engineering fundamentals and the ability to learn quickly across the stack matter most.

What success looks like

  • You can independently deliver scoped features and fixes across the backend and supporting web applications.
  • Your changes are understandable, tested, and documented, with appropriate attention to security and compatibility.
  • You help make processing pipelines and production services more reliable and easier to troubleshoot.
  • You contribute constructively to reviews, communicate progress and blockers, and help the team turn research ideas into maintainable software.

What we offer

  • $1500 - $2000 per month, depending on experience.
  • Opportunities for rapid professional growth in a high-impact role: a small team, a live network, and a senior engineer to learn from.
  • Quarterly team retreats in inspiring locations (e.g., Vilnius, Koh Samui).
  • Travel and visa support for business needs.
  • Flexible remote working.


Help us build the data layer that lets AI do science properly.

How to apply


Apply online through the link here: https://airtable.com/appZKkV7FT7eYBhKI/shrjJ3jYfxZjsNckR

It takes about 30 minutes: a few practical questions, four short written answers, links to your code, and your CV or personal website. No cover letter needed.

Applications close on Monday 16 November 2026, 23:59 CET.

We read every application after the deadline and reply to everyone.

Plan staffing against current and forecasted client demand and build the business case for new headcount. This is about changing how the work gets done, not reducing the need for skilled people to do it. A constructive attitude: Attitude is contagious in both directions, across the team and with clients. Full adoption of firm tools and processes: Systems are critical to growth and often fail to be effective when only part of the team uses them well. jobs.description:
Working for a company like Smile Digital Health means supporting our mandate for #BetterGlobalHealth . We strive towards this goal every day, and the results can be seen in the impact of our innovative health data platform and data management solutions, which are used in over 20 countries. We were #19 on Deloitte's Technology Fast 50 Ranking for 2024! Smile Digital Health makes it easy for healthcare stakeholders to collect and exchange data with our leading FHIR-based data liberation platform. At its heart, the Smile platform enables people and organizations to better manage healthcare data. We help generate and liberate structured healthcare data to ensure effective delivery across care teams and health systems bringing #BetterGlobalHealth to patients everyday! Apply today and find plenty of reasons to SMILE! The Cloud Engineer (Automation) is responsible for designing, building, operating and improving production-grade automation for Smile Digital Health, its clients and partners. This role will be responsible for the pipelines, infrastructure as code, environments and recovery procedures, that the platform runs on. This Engineer will merge direct platform engineering expertise with driving strategic changes in how the department designs, deploys, and maintains its infrastructure. Key responsibilities include managing build and release engineering, orchestrating the Terraform and Helm infrastructure, provisioning on-demand environments, and implementing automated recovery. This role works closely with Platform Engineering, Solution Engineering, Service Operations and Engineering Practice & QA to remove unnecessary repetitive, manual work and effectively optimize a build from the time the client commits to a running environment faster, decrease platform costs, and utilize AI to enhance the platformâs engineering and operations. 
 Responsibilities: Own build and release engineering by reviewing the current repositories and CI setup, then consolidate duplicated Azure DevOps pipeline YAML onto shared reusable templates with change detection and automated quality gates. Identify and eliminate manual efforts for cross-functional teams and replace them with scheduled, auditable automation. For example, automating patching, certificate and secret rotation, environment scaling, and recurring reports Implement GitOps-based continuous delivery - declarative, Git-driven deployments with automated reconciliation, drift detection and rollback. Automate line-of-business environments end to end, provisioned and torn down on demand across every Azure service and application involved. Automate business continuity and disaster recovery through backup validation, restore and failover, recurring DR drills, and measured RTO and RPO. Ensure Helm and Terraform are easy to upgrade by charting reuse and configuration validation, versioned modules, and state boundaries that limit how far an upgrade reaches. Run in-cluster platform services deployed through Helm, harden workloads for availability and capacity: health probes, replica counts, and right-sized requests, limits and autoscaling. Ensure that the Terraform configuration is regularly maintained. Build and maintain Build Agent images for streamlining tooling available for the builds. Automate the guardrails such as policy-as-code, security and IaC scanning in the pipeline, and alerts and dashboards defined as code. Implement AI-assisted engineering in the platform teamâs day-to-day work Contribute to the departmentâs AI enablement, package knowledge into reusable skills and runbooks in the shared skill library. Work with the development and operations teams to find automation gaps, prioritize them, and close them. Troubleshoot production and staging issues and document what you automate so others can operate it. Requirements: 6+ years of hands-on cloud engineering, DevOps and/or platform engineering experience, including at least 1-2+ years with infrastructure as code and CI/CD automation on Microsoft Azure in production. Post-secondary education in Computer Science, Engineering, or similar and/or equivalent work experience. Practical in-depth knowledge and expertise in Terraform, Helm and Azure DevOps pipelines, and GitOps delivery (Argo CD or Flux). Strong Terraform skills including, but not limited to, experience with module design, provider version management, state management and refactoring. Expertise in Helm chart authoring and refactoring, including recent experience with Kubernetes and AKS. Demonstrated knowledge across Azure (AKS, Key Vault, Storage, Azure SQL, PostgreSQL, networking, identity) and observability as code (Azure Monitor and/or Grafana, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry). Hands-on experience automating backup, restore and failover with measured RTO and RPO. Hands-on experience with agentic coding tools (Claude Code or equivalent), keeping confidential data out of them and reviewing what they produce. Hands-on experience running, hardening and right-sizing production workloads on Kubernetes Hands-on Kafka operations: topic and partition design, consumer group sizing, and throughput and latency trade-offs. Experience migrating between Kafka platforms (HDInsight, Confluent, MSK or self-managed) is a strong asset. Strong Python and Bash skills, able to build maintainable tooling, not glue scripts. A demonstrable record of replacing manual processes with automation. FinOps practice and Azure Cost Management, an asset. Regulated environment experience (healthcare, PHI), an asset. Certifications: HashiCorp Terraform Associate; Microsoft AZ-104, AZ-400, AZ-305; CKA or CKAD, an asset. Observability as code with Azure Monitor, Grafana, Prometheus, or OpenTelemetry; Azure cost optimization, an asset. 
 $120,000 - $140,000 a year 
 Smile discloses that artificial intelligence (AI) may be used in portions of the recruitment and selection process, such as resume screening or application assessment. All hiring decisions are ultimately made by qualified human decision-makers, and AI tools are used to support â not replace â fair and equitable hiring practices. This position is a new role, created to support Smileâs continued growth and commitment to operational excellence. Some of the benefits we offer: * Remote Work Environment * Flexible Time Away From Work Policy including PTO, Personal and Sick Days * Competitive Salary and Health/Medical Benefits * RRSP/TFSA/401K Employee Contribution * Life and Disability * Employee Assistance Program * FHIR Study Program and Skillsoft Learning * Super HAPI Fun Club Smile's core values include respect, inclusion, embracing our differences, and celebrating shared values because our people are the foundation of our success. We are big on creating a sense of belonging and empowering each other to bring our authentic selves to work. We are dedicated to fostering a workplace that values diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome and encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply. Candidates are encouraged to inform us if they wish to discuss or require accommodations during interviews or while working at Smile. Consequential Work. Dedicated People.


About Onebrief

Onebrief builds collaboration and AI-powered workflow software for military planning and operational coordination.

Military planning is complex by nature, requiring teams to coordinate information, people, and decisions across systems and locations. Onebrief brings planning, collaboration, simulation, and AI into one connected environment, helping teams test strategies, adapt to changing conditions, and make decisions with greater clarity when the stakes are real.

We are a distributed team of builders from military, operational, and technology backgrounds who care deeply about improving how important work gets done. Some team members work remotely, while others work directly alongside customers in operational environments around the world.

Founded in 2019, Onebrief is backed by leading investors including General Catalyst, Battery Ventures, Insight Partners, Sapphire Ventures, and Human Capital. Valued at more than $2 billion, we continue to invest in product innovation, AI capabilities, and team growth.

Why This Role Exists

As a Solutions Engineer at Onebrief, you work where mission, engineering, and compliance meet.

You'll own technical solution design and deployment readiness, translating customer requirements into secure, scalable deployment architectures. You'll partner with Platform Engineering, SRE, and our Cybersecurity team to validate infrastructure, configure environments, resolve technical blockers, and successfully transition solutions into production.

Youâll work with our go-to-market and customer facing teams to meet with planners, operations officers, and network owners to understand how they work today. Youâll help show them what that work looks like in Onebrief, and then you'll make it real.

You connect a staff's planning problem to a live, accredited Onebrief deployment.

What You'll Do

Core responsibilities:

  • Run technical discovery. With Sales and Engineering, map a staff's current workflow and pain points, specifically focusing on their technical constraints: networks, hosting, identity, and integration requirements, especially in multi-network environments.

  • Lead deployment engineering. Coordinate the technical delivery of new deployments, including infrastructure validation, network configuration checks, and system readiness verification. Write code to configure new deployments and support new environments.

  • Support accreditation. Help create and review security documentation, including STIG checklists and ATO artifacts, alongside our cybersecurity team so deployments are accredited on the customer's timeline.

  • Align stakeholders. Get technical stakeholders on both sides to agree on requirements, constraints, and tradeoffs, so customers see value sooner. Ensure those technical requirements are properly translated into contract deliverables.

  • Scope integrations. Design how Onebrief Connect fits into a command's ecosystem: APIs, data pipelines, Foundry and Maven Smart System, CUOPS tools, and dashboards.

  • Deliver tailored demos. Lead technical demonstrations and solution validation, partnering with Sales and customer-facing teams to demonstrate Onebrief's technical capabilities, deployment architecture, security posture, and integration options.

  • Run pilot deployments. Configure Onebrief in new and untested environments to enable limited uses in support of new sales.

  • Turn field experience into patterns. Convert what you learn in deployments into structured workflows and reusable implementation patterns, and feed clear requirements to Product and Engineering.

  • Travel 30â50% of the time to customer sites and exercises.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility.

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

  • 4+ years in solutions engineering, infrastructure or deployment engineering, or forward-deployed engineering, working closely with go-to-market and operational teams

  • Experience in DoW environments and their security and compliance requirements (RMF, STIGs, ICD 503)

  • Strong expertise with containers (Docker) and orchestration (Kubernetes)

  • Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) and on-premises virtualization (RHEL)

  • Solid understanding of networking concepts and protocols, and of security best practices for highly sensitive environments

  • Strong presence with customers, from action officers to senior leaders, and clear, concise writing

  • Calm under pressure, and focused on forward motion

  • Proficiency in a scripting language (Python, Go, or Bash)

  • Infrastructure as code (Terraform, CloudFormation, Ansible)

  • Monitoring and logging tools (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK, Datadog) and service mesh (Istio, Linkerd)

jobs.title: Graduate Transport Planner
jobs.description:
At Curtins, we're an employee-owned engineering consultancy driven by a simple ambition: to create a better built environment for everyone.

For over 65 years, we've delivered practical, innovative and sustainable solutions that make a positive impact on communities across the UK and Ireland. From major regeneration schemes and commercial developments to education, healthcare and residential projects, our work helps shape the places where people live, learn, work and thrive.

As a Graduate Transport Planner, you'll work alongside experienced planners, engineers and consultants, contributing to a wide range of projects while developing the technical and professional skills you need to build your career.

Whether you're interested in transport assessments, active travel & sustainable mobility, highways or public transport, we'll give you the experience, guidance and support to find the areas that interest you most and develop your expertise in development planning.

What you'll be doing

You will support the planning and development process, helping clients bring projects forward from initial concept through to planning approval.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Assisting with the preparation of Transport Assessments and Transport Statements.

  • Supporting the production of Travel Plans and technical planning reports.

  • Analysing traffic, transport and movement data.

  • Assisting with junction assessments and development impact studies.

  • Supporting planning applications for residential, commercial and mixed-use developments.

  • Working alongside planners, civil engineers and other specialists to deliver integrated solutions.

  • Attending client meetings, project discussions and stakeholder consultations.

  • Taking part in wider Curtins activities including STEM outreach, charity initiatives and community projects.

What kind of projects will I get to work on?

You'll be involved in projects across a wide range of sectors, including:

  • Residential developments.

  • Urban regeneration schemes.

  • Commercial and industrial projects.

  • Education and healthcare developments.

  • Mixed-use masterplans.

  • Strategic land and development opportunities.

You'll help assess how developments interact with the transport network and support clients through the planning process, helping turn ideas into deliverable projects.

How will Curtins support my development?

Our goal is simple: to help you become the best engineer you can be.

Through the Curtins Graduate Academy, you'll follow a structured development programme designed to accelerate both your technical and professional growth.

You'll benefit from:

  • A structured graduate development programme.

  • Dedicated mentoring and coaching.

  • Regular technical and professional skills training.

  • Support towards professional registration and Chartership.

  • Exposure to a wide range of projects, clients and sectors.

  • Opportunities to build your network across the business.

You'll be supported by experienced professionals who are genuinely invested in your success and development.

What we're looking for

We're looking for graduates who are curious, analytical and interested in how development projects are planned and delivered.

You'll ideally be studying towards or have recently completed a degree in:

  • Transport Planning

  • Geography

  • Urban Planning

  • Civil Engineering

  • Town Planning

  • Geography or a related discipline

It would also be advantageous to hold an MSc in Transport Planning, Transport Engineering, Urban Planning, or Development Planning.

Most importantly, we're looking for people who share our values:

Integrity - Doing the right thing.

Being Human - Supporting and respecting others.

Curiosity - Asking questions and seeking better solutions.

Impact - Making a meaningful difference through our work.

Why join Curtins?

As an employee-owned business, every person at Curtins contributes to and benefits from our success.

Alongside exciting projects and a supportive culture, you'll enjoy:

  • Industry-leading benefits package.

  • Award-winning training and development programmes.

  • Employee ownership benefits.

  • Opportunities to get involved in STEM, charity and community initiatives.

  • Access to our unique Employee Extras, including our 5-star holiday lodges.

Most importantly, you'll be joining a business where your ideas matter, your development is supported and your contribution makes a real difference.

Build your future with Curtins.

Should you wish to discuss any adjustments to the application process or provide us with feedback please contact hr@curtins.com we would be happy to discuss ways we can make the process more suitable to your needs.

We value diversity and respect all differences in people. We invite enthusiastic individuals who share in our values of teamwork, client focus, integrity, and quality to apply to join us.

We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.

You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.

Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.


How it works

  1. Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.
  2. Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.

  • Regular use of an AI coding tool
  • Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models
  • You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words
  • At least 10 hours a week, starting now

Nice to have

  • Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure

Terms

Original job posting link

garden3d TK â Media

Mill

Your Opportunity

Working cross-functionally with Data Engineering, Product, Clinical Operations, and EMR partners, your solutions will transform how clinicians access dataâmoving from external tools and workarounds to seamless, in-workflow decision support via CDS Hooks and real-time APIs.

You will own the technical foundation for Clinical Decision Support (CDS) Hooks, REST APIs, and the architectural patterns that ensure clinical data is accessible, trustworthy, and performant at the moment of care. This role sits at the intersection of healthcare interoperability standards, modern API design, and operational excellence. You will establish reliability metrics and SLAs that ensure CDS Hooks and APIs serve clinician workflows with consistent quality and performance. You will be part of a small, high-performing healthcare engineering team where engineers support each other's growth through mentorship and tight collaboration.

  • Lead design and implementation of the CDS Hooks platform, including card orchestration, hook context handling, EHR-side logic orchestration, and integration with downstream data services

  • Define and measure clinical impact metrics â adoption of CDS Hooks, clinician interaction rates, workflow integration success, and patient outcome influence

  • Establish and uphold engineering standards for API design, data schemas, integration patterns, and interoperability; maintain high-quality technical documentation and OpenAPI specifications

  • Partner with Data Engineering to align upstream data models, gold-layer datasets, and platform capabilities with clinical decision support and API requirements

  • 2+ years of hands-on experience with CDS Hooks, SMART on FHIR, or similar clinical decision support APIs

  • Strong experience designing and operating REST APIs, including contract design, versioning, error handling, and authentication/authorization patterns

  • Deep understanding of healthcare data integrations, EMR workflows, and interoperability patterns (FHIR, HL7, CDS Hooks, SMART on FHIR)

  • Expertise in designing for reliability, SLAs, and operational metrics; ability to translate clinical requirements into technical SLOs

  • Experience defining and measuring API performance metrics (latency, availability, error rates); familiarity with SLA monitoring and enforcement

  • Strong systems thinking with ability to design for scale, reliability, maintainability, and resilience

jobs.description: QuickMail is a cold email and LinkedIn outreach platform for markets you can't afford to burn. Our customers can't easily replace leads that land in spam, which is why deliverability matters more to us than anything else. We have been running since 2014, and we pioneered deliverability technology such as Inbox rotationâ¢ and deliverability AIâ¢. The Role We are hiring a technical customer support person with an owner's mentality. You will own support for QuickMail and Mailflow, our deliverability add-on. There is no first or second line. You are the first and last person our customers talk to. Customers count on you to solve their problems and find the real cause when something breaks. You work closely with engineering, and you tell the founder what we need to know to make the product better: where the friction is and where the opportunities are. The role covers the help desk, system health checks, testing new releases before they ship, and leading the weekly team meeting. It takes excellent communication, solid technical understanding and sharp critical thinking. This is not a script-reading job. Most tickets involve deliverability, DNS records, LinkedIn automation or campaign setup. You dig into customer accounts in our Support Dashboard, reproduce the issue, then decide what to do and how to explain it to the customer. We are a remote team spread across time zones. Most routine tasks have a written guide with a checklist, so you know what done looks like. You are expected to refine and improve those processes. When something new comes up, you work out the most efficient way to handle it. If you want a lot of autonomy across many areas, real responsibility and a fast-paced environment, this role is for you. What Work Looks Like You own two things: customers get unstuck fast, and the product stays reliable. Every day Set the day's support priorities and work the Help Scout queue for QuickMail and Mailflow. Triage, resolve, and dig deeper when a ticket needs it. Check the support dashboard: job queue, event-stream latency, blacklist status, newly purchased domains. If something is off, investigate, diagnose, and drive it to resolution. Review fraud alerts and disable accounts that are scams or abusing the platform. Delighting customers Comfortable jumping on calls with customers, building rapport fast, and setting them up for success. Update the changelog and help articles based on what shipped and what customers asked. Share customer feedback with the team, ask happy customers for reviews and case studies, and watch NPS for testimonial candidates. Making support smarter with AI Improve the AI support agent. Review its answers, fix the docs it drew from when it is wrong, and contact the customer when its reply was off. Write and maintain automated tests, built with AI, that try to break staging before customers do. Use the MCP connections we have in place (Helpscout, GitHub, Postmark, and others) to get an accurate picture of support and find the next thing worth improving. Keeping the product solid Gatekeep releases. New fixes and features land on staging every week. Test them, confirm when staging is ready to ship, and think through how existing and new users will be affected. Report bugs as GitHub issues with everything the developer needs: steps to reproduce, screenshots or a Loom, and any GraphQL or console errors. Captain red alerts. When a core feature breaks (emails not sending, login down), confirm it, alert the team on Slack or Telegram, update the status page every 30 minutes, keep affected customers informed, and drive the fix. Then run the retrospective so it does not happen twice. Running the week Lead the weekly team meeting in MonsterOps: issues written up, to-dos done, numbers updated. Keep rock status and KPIs current in MonsterOps. Tools you'll use: Helpscout, our Support Dashboard, Sidekiq, GitHub, Slack, Telegram, MonsterOps, Outline, MxToolbox, Postmark, Bento, TidyCal, Fathom, Visual Code and Claude. Who You Are You build rapport fast. You are warm, positive, and relatable in writing and on calls. You are a good communicator. Externally, you can show warmth, empathy and care. Internally, you are able to communicate clearly and concisely about important things. You can operate with minimal instructions. You understand a short brief without every detail spelled out. You can prioritize well (especially when you have a lot on your plate), and get things done without hand-holding. You are comfortable on video. You are natural on live calls with Zoom and Meet, and on recorded video through tools like Loom. Your teammates can always count on you. You say what you'll do and you do what you said. You act with a constant sense of urgency. You can execute fast and find new ways to improve your productivity. You are resourceful. You use all the tools at your disposal to get great results. You have a low ego. You don't take offense easily and you handle disagreement as a discussion, not a personal attack. Growth mindset. You are positive about new workflow/process/product/tool changes. You love giving and receiving positive and negative feedback without getting defensive. Hours that overlap with East coast US and UK, where most of our customers are. A Plus If You Have Experience with customer facing work, or if you don't have it, tell us why you are perfect for this role. Working knowledge of deliverability and LinkedIn outreach. Warmup, DNS, inbox rotation, DKIM, SPF, Outlook and Gmail technical setup. We can teach this, but a head start helps. Comfort with agency setups. Workspaces, guest seats, inbox purchases and what happens when an agency loses a client. Light data skills. You can pull numbers from Help Scout or our MCP to back up what you report. An eye for happy customers. You notice them and ask for testimonials and case studies at the right moment. How We Work Together You'll work directly with the founder and with our lead developer. Working with the founder can be intense. Here is what that looks like in practice: Replies are short and can come across as harsh. If something written lands badly or isn't clear, ask. Direction can change. The founder may say one thing, then something different a few days later as they learn more. When that happens, check what changed and adapt. Information should be short and to the point. Lead with what matters, then give more details if asked. The founder can stay frustrated about a problem until it's solved. That's something they are aware of and working on. You'll do well here if you can stay calm and focused when the pressure is on. This role suits someone with high emotional intelligence, who doesn't take things personally, asks when something is unclear, and keeps many things moving at once. Your schedule can be flexible. If you have a martial arts class every Thursday at 3 pm, go and make up the time later. In return, on the rare occasion the team needs your help on a weekend, we ask you to be flexible too.   • Work with SIHO Legal and key leadership on special cases and external inquiries from CMS, the Indiana Department of Insurance, law enforcement, and others

  • Ability to work successfully under tight deadlines
  • Experience with SIHO systems including the HSP claims system
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office suite products including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook

raw_payload.description:
Job Title: Patient Care Advocate 

Job Location: Remote


About Us: 

We are a dedicated team focused on improving access to affordable prescription medications for patients. By partnering with insurance companies, healthcare providers, and pharmacies, we work to reduce the financial burden of medications, ensuring that patients can access the treatments they need without excessive costs. 


Role Overview: 

As a key member of our team, you will help patients navigate our Prescription Payment Plan. This involves working closely with patients, insurance providers, healthcare professionals, and pharmacies to ensure seamless enrollment, eligibility verification, cost-sharing, and prescription fulfillment. 


What You’ll Do: 

  • Patient Enrollment & Eligibility: Assist patients with enrolling in the program, ensuring all necessary personal and insurance information is provided and verifying eligibility. 
  • Prescription Coverage: Help patients confirm that their prescribed medications are covered under the program, and manage the approval process for eligible medications. 
  • Cost-Sharing & Payment: Reduce patients' out-of-pocket costs by applying the program benefits. Manage copayments, coinsurance, and assist with additional copay assistance when applicable. 
  • Prescription Fulfillment: Coordinate with participating pharmacies to ensure the correct application of benefits during prescription filling, ensuring patients pay the reduced amount. 
  • Refills & Continued Use: Support patients by ensuring they continue receiving medications at reduced costs, monitoring adherence to medication regimens, and ensuring continued eligibility. 
  • Program Renewal & Updates: Guide patients through annual renewals and inform them about any updates to the program or medication formulary. 


What We’re Looking For: 

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Experience in healthcare, insurance or customer service required (experience with prescription assistance programs is a plus)
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to navigate complex processes
  • Excellent communication skills for working with patients, healthcare providers, and pharmacies
  • A genuine passion for helping others and making a positive impact on their healthcare access
  • The ability to work efficiently and collaboratively within a team environment

Success Factors for Working from Home 

  • Private Workspace: A dedicated, quiet workspace with a door that closes, free from ambient noise. 
  • Ergonomics: A comfortable desk and chair setup that allows for the proper installation of necessary equipment. 
  • Reliable Internet Connection: Stable, high-speed internet with a minimum bandwidth of 10 Mbps downstream and 5 Mbps upstream. 
  • Quiet, Distraction-Free Workspace: A dedicated, quiet area where you can focus on delivering excellent customer service without interruptions. 
  • Tech-Savvy: Comfort with technology and ability to learn new systems quickly. 
  • Self-motivation & Independence: Ability to stay productive and manage your time effectively in a remote environment. 
  • Communication Skills: Strong verbal and written communication skills, especially in a virtual setting. 
  • Adaptability: Ability to adapt to changing technologies and procedures while working remotely. 


Compensation & Perks 

  • Hourly Pay: $16.50 per hour 
  • Company-Provided Equipment: All necessary equipment will be provided. 
  • Comprehensive Benefits: Full health insurance package including medical, dental, and vision coverage. 
  • Cell Phone Benefits: $25/month per line for unlimited phone, text, and data (restrictions may apply). 
  • Generous Referral Program: Earn $50 per paycheck for every person you refer—and your referral earns it too! No limits on payouts. 
  • Comprehensive Training: Paid training to ensure you are fully prepared for success. 
  • Career Growth: Opportunities for career advancement and professional development within a leading healthcare provider. 
  • Work-from-Home Convenience: Save time, and money, and reduce your environmental footprint. 
  • Inclusive Culture: We are an Equal Opportunity Employer, including individuals with disabilities and veterans. 

What Success Looks Like: 

  • Reduced out-of-pocket costs for patients through effective cost-sharing and copay assistance 
  • Timely and accurate processing of prescription claims and approvals 
  • High patient satisfaction with the program’s support and streamlined experience 
  • Compliance with program requirements and monitoring of patient eligibility for ongoing assistance 

Why Join Us? 

  • Be part of a team that makes a real difference in patients' lives by reducing the cost of necessary medications 
  • Opportunity for professional growth in the healthcare and insurance sectors 
  • Competitive compensation and benefits package 
  • A collaborative, supportive, and innovative work culture 

Ready to Make an Impact? 

Join us in making prescription medications more affordable and accessible for those who need them most. If you're ready to help make a difference, we'd love to hear from you! 

If you like wild growth and working with happy, enthusiastic over-achievers, you'll enjoy your career with us!

You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.

 

Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.

 

How it works

 

  1. Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.
  2. Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.
  3. Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks.
  4. Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.
  5. Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.
  6. Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.
  7. Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another.

  • 2+ years of professional software engineering
  • Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code)

Nice to have

Terms

jobs.title: 3P Revenue Accounting & Reporting
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

We are looking for a Senior Manager, 3P Revenue Accounting & Reporting to join our Accounting team. You will own revenue recognition, month-end close and reporting for Claude sold through our cloud service provider (CSP) channels: AWS Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI and Microsoft Azure Marketplace. These channels are among the fastest-growing revenue streams at the company. They run on consumption-based, partner-reported data that changes every month.

You will be the accounting point of contact for the finance and partner teams at AWS, Google and Microsoft. Internally, you will partner with Finance, FAB, Engineering and business teams to turn partner billing feeds into accurate, auditable revenue. You will also lead the automation of a close that is still heavily manual. If you want to build the financial infrastructure behind a fast-growing AI company, come join us in our mission to build safe, beneficial AI.

Key responsibilities

  • Lead the revenue close for cloud service provider Marketplace within a listed company timeline.

  • Prepare and review revenue, revenue-share, reserve journal entries, accruals and true-ups including memos for accounting assessments and judgments.

  • Own balance sheet reconciliations, reserves, and the usage-to-invoice-to-cash bridge.

  • Perform monthly and quarterly flux analysis and prepare flux decks for leadership.

  • Own quarter-end deliverables, including footnote disclosures, flux commentary and presentations to leadership and Corporate Accounting.

  • Serve as the primary contact for external auditors.

  • Review the work of accountants and contractors, set the close calendar, and keep close packages complete and audit-ready.

  • Own monthly and quarterly 3P revenue reporting for leadership and FP&A, by partner, model, product, region and customer.

  • Review partner usage, invoice, disbursement and fraud reports each month, and resolve data issues before close.

  • Serve as the accounting point of contact for the finance, engineering and product teams and drive reporting improvements that support an on-time close.

  • Apply ASC 606 to 3P arrangements, including principal-vs-agent, variable consideration and reseller arrangements.

  • Estimate and document reserves, including credit loss (ASC 326).

  • Assess the accounting for new 3P products, programs and billing changes, partnering with Technical Accounting on complex judgments.

  • Partner with the Engineering teams to automate manual close processes, including SQL-driven workbooks, automated reconciliations and system-generated journal entries.

  • Own 3P SOX controls, including design, documentation, gap remediation and audit evidence.

  • Partner with FP&A, Treasury, AR and business teams on forecasts, cash and partner disputes.

Minimum qualifications

  • Have strong ASC 606 knowledge, especially principal-vs-agent, variable consideration, consideration payable to a customer, and consumption-based revenue.

  • Have owned a month-end close with tight deadlines and reviewed journal entries, reconciliations and flux analysis.

  • Have built revenue reporting from large, imperfect third-party data sets and reconciled it to the general ledger.

  • Have managed external partner relationships where you depended on their data, and pushed for fixes.

  • Have strong SQL skills (BigQuery or similar) and experience automating close workbooks or reconciliations.

  • Have designed or operated SOX controls and supported external audits.

  • Communicate clearly with accounting, finance, business and engineering teams.

  • Thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments where processes are still being built.

Preferred qualifications

  • Have 10+ years of progressive accounting experience, including 3+ years managing revenue accounting or close teams.

  • A Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance; CPA or equivalent (ACA, ACCA).

  • Big 4 audit experience combined with industry experience at a high-growth tech or SaaS company.

  • Experience with cloud marketplace, reseller or channel revenue (AWS Marketplace, Google Cloud Marketplace, Azure Marketplace).

  • Experience with usage-based and subscription revenue models.

  • Hands-on experience with Workday Financials, NetSuite, Numeric, Hex or similar close and reporting tools.

  • Experience with IPO readiness.

  • Experience using AI tools to automate accounting and reporting work.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$190,000—$230,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. jobs.title: Activation Manager, Beneficial Deployments
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As a Deployment Manager on the Beneficial Deployments team, you will guide customers from a signed contract into a live, governed, and adopted deployment so that customers achieve tangible impact rather than simply incremental improvement with Claude. You'll guide organizations from contract signature to production deployment across Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, and our API products, fundamentally changing how they work and deliver on their missions.

You'll be the technical hands that switch Claude on. Before any organization can drive adoption, before any champion can ship their first workflow, someone has to connect Claude to the customer's identity provider, get the right people provisioned into the right workspaces, and walk their CISO through how it all comes together. That's your work. You turn "we've signed the contract" into "our employees can log in, with the right access, under the right policies, the way our security team expects."

This is a high-leverage role where you'll pioneer scalable activation methodologies that enable hundreds of nonprofit customers to unlock transformative use cases and realize measurable outcomes at unprecedented speed. You won't just follow playbooks. You'll design the frameworks and repeatable processes that can be deployed consistently across diverse customer environments, and you'll shape them into programs that reach customers we could never serve one at a time.

You'll operate at the intersection of technical deployment, enablement, and program design. Some days you'll be in the weeds with a customer's IT team debugging a SAML assertion; other days you'll be stepping back to ask how the last ten deployments should change the next hundred. Your systems-thinking approach will directly shape how we activate customers, and your strategic management will ensure every customer achieves meaningful outcomes within their first 90 days. By identifying patterns across activations, you'll build replicable approaches to organizational change while maintaining the agility to customize solutions for each customer's unique transformation journey.

Responsibilities:

  • Own the complete activation journey from contract signature to production deployment, orchestrating cross-functional resources and customer teams to ensure rapid time-to-value across Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, and API products.

  • Deploy Claude inside customer environments. Configure and troubleshoot SSO (SAML), SCIM and JIT provisioning, MCP connectors, admin policy templates, and seat-assignment logic across Okta, Entra ID, Ping, and Google Workspace. Deliver informative transitions to Support for deeper issues that require investigation or engineering support.

  • Act as a trusted advisor to customer CISOs and CTOs on governance and enterprise setup. Bring a clear point of view on best practices, help security and IT leadership make the design decisions that determine whether a deployment holds up over time

  • Light up the capabilities that make Claude valuable. Enable and govern MCP connectors to the customer's systems, ensure Skills, Projects, and other capabilities are turned on and configured for their use cases, and work with their IT team on the approvals and OAuth consent this requires, so that day one feels ready

  • Design and scale activation frameworks by identifying patterns across deployments and building templated playbooks that balance standardization with customization for breakthrough outcomes.

  • Turn playbooks into programs. Package what works into repeatable, increasingly self-serve motions (deployment checklists, admin enablement sessions, onboarding cohorts, Claude-powered guidance) so that activation quality no longer depends on you being in the room.

  • Drive organizational transformation by developing change management strategies, rollout plans, and Train-the-Trainer programs that build internal AI champions and catalyze adoption across customer organizations.

  • Define and track success metrics across activation rate, time-to-value, customer satisfaction, and operational efficiency, using data to continuously optimize the motion.

  • Channel customer insights back to Product, Support, and Security teams, serving as voice of the customer so that repeat deployment blockers get solved once.

You may be a good fit if you have:

  • 5+ years in customer-facing technical roles such as implementation management, technical account management, technical onboarding, solutions consulting, or customer success, with a track record of running multiple concurrent enterprise deployments with documented handoffs.

  • Experience serving nonprofits or mission-driven organizations. You've worked with (or inside) them and you understand how they differ from commercial enterprises. 

  • Hands-on, sustained ownership of enterprise identity integration work. SAML, OIDC, SCIM v2, and JIT provisioning across at least two major identity providers (Okta, Entra ID, Ping, Google Workspace). You can debug a broken SAML assertion or a misconfigured SCIM attribute map without escalating, and you know when a Support handoff is the right call.

  • Experience advising CISOs, CTOs, or IT leadership on enterprise governance and setup for a SaaS or AI platform, with an informed point of view on org topology, access models, RBAC, and OAuth. 

  • Working knowledge of security and compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR) sufficient to anticipate what a customer's security review will ask, and to know when to bring in our AI Security Specialist.

About the Role

Anthropic runs one of the largest and fastest-growing infrastructure fleets in the industry, across multiple accelerator families, CPU families, clouds, neoclouds, and on-prem sites. Capacity Engineering owns the data, tooling, and systems that let Anthropic plan, measure, and maximize utilization of that fleet: we partner on supply deals, wire telemetry from day zero, own the canonical capacity data layer, and build the planning and enforcement tools every research and product team relies on. This role sits in the Planning pillar, on the Demand Planning team, and works daily with research engineering, pretraining, inference, compute supply, finance, and external vendors.

You own the tranches. The job has two halves that feed each other. Upstream, you take the Demand Planning forecast and turn it into per-tranche requirements — shape, interconnect, region, supporting resources, date — and carry those into sourcing negotiations and data center build reviews so we contract for capacity we can actually use when we need it. Downstream, you own the integrated schedule and system of record for every tranche in flight — from contracted through reserved, ingested, in-cluster, healthy, and occupied — and you drive the owners of each hop to their dates. Every slip you see downstream becomes a contract-language fix, an automation, or a correction fed back to the forecast.

What you'll do

  • Turn the forecast into per-tranche requirements. Take the Demand Planning forecast plus direct input from research, pretraining, and inference planners, and convert it into concrete accelerator, interconnect, region, supporting-resource, and date requirements for each tranche. Represent those in sourcing negotiations and data center build reviews, including which contractual terms actually move delivery dates.
  • Qualify tranches for deliverability before signature. The Capacity Planner signs fit-to-forecast; you sign whether the shape can land schedulable, healthy, and instrumented in that region on that date, with storage, egress, identity in place.
  • Close the delivery loop. Track forecast-versus-delivered on shape, region, and timing for every tranche; publish the variance; and feed it back to Demand Planning and into the next contract.
  • Own the bring-up system of record. Define the canonical contract-to-occupied state machine with explicit entry and exit criteria per stage, and make it a first-class object in the capacity data layer so every downstream tool sees in-flight capacity, not only what has landed.
  • Run a portfolio of bring-ups in parallel — new cloud regions, on-prem sites, neocloud blocks — with one integrated schedule spanning provider milestones, cluster creation, network turn-up, storage readiness, health burn-in, and first-workload landing. 
  • Drive readiness automation: All capacity systems are fully integrated for all new capacity, from contracted through ingested, automated and scaled.
  • Instrument and publish the numbers that matter — time-to-occupied and paid-idle dollars per tranche — with executive-level reporting on status, tradeoffs, and risk across the portfolio.

  • Significant experience delivering large-scale infrastructure — cloud regions, accelerator clusters, HPC systems, or bare-metal fleets — at multi-region scale or ≥10k accelerators (or CPU/storage equivalent).

  • SQL and enough Python to answer your own questions and build your own reporting.
  • A degree in a technical field or an equivalent engineering track record.

  • Reserved-capacity onboarding, private offers, or capacity commitments with cloud or neocloud providers.
  • Enough demand-planning exposure to challenge a forecast, translate it into per-tranche requirements, and feed delivery variance back into it.
  • Data center or colocation delivery: power and space planning, network turn-up, site acceptance, vendor management.
  • Accelerator health and burn-in, collective-communications sanity testing, or fleet-health SLOs — and a rigorous definition of "healthy."
  • Systems of record or lifecycle services for infrastructure assets.
  • Onboarding a new hardware generation into an existing scheduler and observability stack.

Anthropic Fellows Program overview

The Anthropic Fellows Program is designed to foster AI research and engineering talent. We provide funding and mentorship to promising technical talent - regardless of previous experience.

Fellows will primarily use external infrastructure (e.g. open-source models, public APIs) to work on an empirical project aligned with our research priorities, with the goal of producing a public output (e.g. a paper submission). In one of our earlier cohorts, over 80% of fellows produced papers. We run multiple cohorts of Fellows each year and review applications on a rolling basis.

What to expect

  • 4 months of full-time research 
  • Direct mentorship from Anthropic researchers 
  • Access to a shared workspace (in either Bay Area, California, Toronto, Canada, or London, UK)
  • Connection to the broader AI safety and security research community
  • Weekly stipend of 3,850 USD / 2,310 GBP / 4,300 CAD + benefits (these vary by country)
  • Funding for compute (~$15k/month) and other research expenses

Interview process

The interview process will include an initial application & reference check, technical assessments & interviews, and a research discussion. 

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Compensation

The expected base stipend for this role is 3,850 USD / 2,310 GBP / 4,300 CAD per week, with an expectation of 40 hours per week for 4 months (with possible extension).

Across the workstreams, you may be a good fit if you:

  • Are motivated by making sure AI is safe and beneficial for society as a whole
  • Are excited to transition into empirical AI research and would be interested in a full-time role at Anthropic
  • Have a strong technical background in computer science, mathematics, or physics
  • Thrive in fast-paced, collaborative environments
  • Can implement ideas quickly and communicate clearly

Strong candidates may also have:

  • Strong background in a discipline relevant to a specific Fellows workstream (e.g. economics, social sciences, or cybersecurity)
  • Experience in areas of research or engineering related to their workstream

Candidates must be:

  • Fluent in Python programming
  • Available to work full-time on the Fellows program

AI Safety Fellows

Mentors, research areas, & past projects

Fellows will undergo a project selection & mentor matching process. Potential mentors include:

  • Sam Bowman
  • Sara Price
  • Alex Tamkin
  • Nina Panickssery
  • Trenton Bricken
  • Logan Graham
  • Jascha Sohl-Dickstein
  • Joe Benton
  • Collin Burns
  • Fabien Roger
  • Samuel Marks
  • Kyle Fish
  • Ethan Perez

Our mentors will lead projects in select AI safety research areas, such as:

  • Scalable Oversight: Developing techniques to keep highly capable models helpful and honest, even as they surpass human-level intelligence in various domains.
  • Adversarial Robustness and AI Control: Creating methods to ensure advanced AI systems remain safe and harmless in unfamiliar or adversarial scenarios.
  • Model Organisms: Creating model organisms of misalignment to improve our empirical understanding of how alignment failures might arise.
  • Model Internals / Mechanistic Interpretability: Advancing our understanding of the internal workings of large language models to enable more targeted interventions and safety measures.
  • AI Welfare: Improving our understanding of potential AI welfare and developing related evaluations and mitigations.

On our Alignment Science and Frontier Red Team blogs, you can read about past projects, including:

  • Subliminal Learning: Language Models Transmit Behavioral Traits via Hidden Signals in Data: Alex Cloud and Minh Le, et al., mentors including Samuel Marks and Owain Evans
  • Open-source circuits: Michael Hanna and Mateusz Piotrowski with mentorship from Emmanuel Ameisen and Jack Lindsey

For a full list of representative projects for each area, please see these blog posts: Introducing the Anthropic Fellows Program for AI Safety Research, Recommendations for Technical AI Safety Research Directions.

Unique candidate criteria

You might be a particularly great fit for this workstream if you:

  • Are motivated by reducing catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems
  • Have experience with empirical ML research projects
  • Have experience working with large language models
  • Have experience in one of the research areas mentioned above
  • Have a track record of open-source contributions

AI Security Fellows

Mentors, research areas, & past projects

Fellows will undergo a project selection & mentor matching process. Potential mentors include:

  • Nicholas Carlini
  • Keri Warr
  • Evyatar Ben Asher
  • Keane Lucas
  • Newton Cheng

On our Alignment Science and Frontier Red Team blogs, you can read about some past Fellows projects, including:

  • AI agents find $4.6M in blockchain smart contract exploits: Winnie Xiao and Cole Killian, mentored by Nicholas Carlini and Alwin Peng
  • Strengthening Red Teams: A Modular Scaffold for Control Evaluations: Chloe Loughridge et al., mentored by Jon Kutasov and Joe Benton

Unique candidate criteria

You might be a particularly great fit for this workstream if you:

  • Are motivated by reducing catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems
  • Have contributed to open-source projects in LLM- or security-adjacent repositories
  • Have demonstrated success in bringing clarity and ownership to ambiguous technical problems
  • Have experience with pentesting, vulnerability research, or other offensive security work
  • Have a demonstrated willingness to do the "dirty work" that produces high-quality outputs
  • Have reported CVEs or been awarded bug bounties
  • Have experience with empirical ML research projects
  • Have experience with deep learning frameworks and experiment management

jobs.title: APAC GTM Enablement Lead
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic’s APAC go-to-market organisation is the fastest-growing part of our international business, spanning markets with distinct languages, cultures and buying styles. Today, enablement for the region is delivered by our global and EMEA teams. As we scale in APAC, we are establishing an initial in-region enablement presence, based in Sydney and supporting the field across the region.

As Enablement Lead, you will be hands-on in getting the APAC field ready: onboarding, ongoing skill development, manager coaching support and launch readiness, across GTM functions, not just sales. You will spend most of your time in the room, running sessions, building programmes and working directly with sellers and managers, in the time zones and languages where customer conversations happen.

This is a build role with a global spine. You inherit a working global and international enablement engine. Your job is to adapt it for APAC, deliver it across the region, and feed what you learn back into the international and global programme.

How we work: adults learn by doing, so we build sessions around live activity: practice, reflection, real customer scenarios. The measure is not what was covered in the room. It is what changes a week later in how people think, decide and sell.

This takes creativity and a solid understanding of how adults learn, applied at speed. The frontier moves quickly and the field is scaling fast. Much of the work is unlearning: helping experienced sellers let go of pre-AI habits, not just teaching new ones. AI is what makes this scalable: endless practice partners, personalised scenarios from real deals, feedback minutes after a call. You will use it that way, not to generate more content.

Key responsibilities

  • Set up the APAC enablement rhythm: in-region onboarding cohorts, live practice-based sessions in APAC time zones, and a feedback loop into the global programme
  • Adapt the international portfolio for APAC, where content for several markets needs to be written and translated ahead of delivery
  • Personally design and facilitate deal walkthroughs, role-plays and customer-conversation rehearsal, favouring practice over presentation
  • Partner with regional GTM leaders to build a coaching standard that scales as the manager layer grows
  • Own launch readiness for the region, so that when a new model or product ships, the APAC field is certified and conversation-ready in the same week cycle as everyone else
  • Build the measurement habit: track what the field does differently afterwards, not content shipped or attendance

Minimum qualifications

  • 8+ years in GTM enablement, sales productivity or similar roles, including experience leading or running enablement programmes
  • Experience delivering GTM enablement in APAC, ideally across more than one of the region’s markets
  • Experience influencing beyond your own team or region, such as a programme adopted elsewhere or a senior stakeholder whose decision you changed
  • Hands-on track record designing and running practice-first enablement, measured by changes in field behaviour
  • A working understanding of how adults learn, and comfort helping experienced sellers unlearn pre-AI habits
  • Creativity with AI in your craft: personalised practice, real-deal scenarios and fast feedback rather than more content
  • Experience owning programmes end to end, from design through delivery and measurement
  • Experience enabling a field across languages and cultures, and knowing what breaks when English-first content ships as-is
  • Comfort working with sales leaders as a peer, including pipeline reviews, deal inspection and forecast conversations
  • Good judgement on when to adapt global programmes and when to adopt them as-is

Strong candidates may also

  • Have held both a global and an APAC enablement role
  • Have run enablement delivered across multiple APAC markets
  • Have helped build or scale an enablement function
  • Have carried a quota or led sellers earlier in their career
  • Have enablement experience in AI, developer platforms or technical products sold to both executives and builders

You'll work directly with flagship research partners like Howard Hughes Medical Institute and The Allen Institute, embedded in their scientific workflows. This isn't consulting from the outside — you'll be building alongside their engineers, prototyping agents that fit into real research pipelines, and developing the ecosystem-level tooling (MCP servers, benchmarks, reusable agent skills) that extends Claude's usefulness across the broader life sciences community.
